ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the three charged small balls A, B, C can be regarded as point charges, carrying charges respectively of ＋Q, －Q, ＋q. A and B are fixed on an insulating horizontal tabletop. C has a small hole and is threaded on a rough insulating rod whose coefficient of kinetic friction is the same everywhere. The insulating rod is placed vertically at the midpoint of the line connecting A and B. C is released from rest from a certain position on the rod, and when it falls to the tabletop its velocity is exactly zero. The charge carried by C remains unchanged as it slides down along the rod. Then during the falling process of C, which of the following judgments is correct?
A. The friction force it experiences becomes larger 
B. The electric field force does positive work
C. The electric potential energy remains unchanged
D. The velocity must be maximum when it has fallen half the height

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the two charged small balls A and B are located on a horizontal tabletop, and there is a line connecting A and B; the insulating rod is placed vertically at the midpoint of the line connecting A and B, and the small ball C is threaded on this vertical rod and moves up and down along the rod. Then reason: Since C always moves on the vertical line through the midpoint of the line connecting A and B, at any moment the distances from C to points A and B are equal; let this be r. In the problem, the charges of A and B are respectively +Q and -Q, so the potential produced by A and B at C is V = kQ/r + k(-Q)/r = 0. The charge of C is +q and remains unchanged during the falling process, so the electric potential energy of C, U = qV, is always 0, that is, it remains the same constant. Therefore during the falling process of C, the electric potential energy remains unchanged.
